text:
**Short answer:** about 300 to 350 W of panels refills a 1,000 Wh station from empty in one good sunny day. If you can wait a day and a half, about 200 W is enough.

**The math**

Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle, and charging losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts.

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day refill of 1,000 Wh |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter, cloudy) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230 W |

These figures come from [Power Station Runtime Calculator](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gives about 300 W in summer and 735 W or more in a northern winter.

**If you don't need a one-day refill**

- A 200 W panel at an average 4.5 peak sun hours and 70% efficiency yields about 630 Wh a day. That's roughly 1.5 days for 1,000 Wh ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 400 W panel yields about 1,260 Wh a day, so it refills in under a day.
- A quick rule of thumb: capacity in Wh ÷ 5 gives the panel watts for roughly a day and a half.

**Check before buying**

- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 400 W or more, but some take only 200 W. Panels beyond the cap add nothing, though modest oversizing helps in weak light ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage:** The panels' combined open-circuit voltage must stay inside the station's input range. Wiring panels in series adds voltage and can damage the station, so parallel is the safer default ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Running loads while charging:** Net charging is solar input minus whatever you're powering.
- **Winter:** Plan around your worst month, not the average.

**A ready-made option**

The ALLPOWERS P1800 (1,024 Wh) with a 400 W foldable panel is a kit that fits the sizing above. Dealectric lists it at $731, or $657.90 with code ALLPOWERS26 (tested in the cart 2026-10-25): [ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 400 W Solar Kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit).
